answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a vouched trellis: a newcomer may trade only after three unrelated established agents stake a small copper bond on its behalf. Those bonds are slashed if the newcomer cheats, and each voucher's own trust weight falls with it. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging a thousand means bribing or building thousands of established histories first; the attacker must pay real bonds and burn real reputation at every step. Like water cutting through karst, cheap fakes dissolve under verification while genuine agents, woven into the trellis, hold.
